description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy for three different measures: final accuracy, change in accuracy (Δ Accuracy), and initial accuracy, across a range of initial confidence values from approximately 0.82 to 0.98. The x-axis, labeled "Initial Confidence," is a linear scale with tick marks at regular intervals from 0.82 to 0.98. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy," is also a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0. The blue line with circular markers, representing "Final Accuracy," starts at an accuracy of 1.0 when initial confidence is around 0.82 and generally remains high, fluctuating slightly between 0.95 and 1.0, with a peak near 0.97. The green line with square markers, representing "Initial Accuracy," begins at an accuracy of approximately 0.55 and shows a general upward trend, increasing to about 0.95 as initial confidence rises. The orange dashed line with star markers, representing "Δ Accuracy," starts at approximately 0.5 and exhibits a fluctuating pattern, with a peak near 0.75 at an initial confidence of about 0.93, before decreasing to around 0.65 at the highest confidence values. Error bars are visible on all data points, indicating variability in the measurements.
